transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 15:00 PT
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Nandi (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (CTO, Ibex), Anya Patel (Head of Security, Ibex), Ethan Cole (SRE, Ibex)

Summary / Purpose: kickoff scoping for a 4-week evaluation pilot; validate security/compliance gates and define benchmark plan and acceptance criteria.

[00:00] Jordan Hale: All right everybody thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour. Quick intros?
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: Marco Ruiz, CTO at Ibex, hey thanks for setting this up.
[00:15] Anya Patel: Anya, head of security. We're mostly concerned with controls for the pilot and what evidence you'll provide.
[00:21] Priya Nandi: Priya from Redwood SE, I'll drive the benchmarking and deployment options.
[00:29] Ethan Cole: Ethan, SRE, I'll own the test harness and telemetry.
[00:33] Jordan Hale: Great. High level goals — Marco, wanted to confirm what success looks like for you for this eval?
[00:43] Marco Ruiz: Two things: one, performance — we need predictable latency under load, p95 ideally under 200ms for our core chat endpoint. Second, security/compliance — we need to see SOC 2 artifacts and be able to authenticate via our IdP (SAML + SCIM), and RBAC so only certain envs can access logs.
[01:02] Priya Nandi: Good, we'll capture those as acceptance gates. For latency - can you share expected qps and payload sizes?
[01:09] Ethan Cole: We're looking at peaks of about 2k requests per minute, so roughly 33 rps sustained; though during peak events we can hit short bursts to 300 rps. Payloads vary, median about 250 token-equivalent, tail up to 1k tokens.
[01:25] Anya Patel: Also need to know how long logs are retained and whether audit logs are searchable and exportable for audits.
[01:31] Jordan Hale: Absolutely. Quick note on hosting: Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), and private VPC/on-prem. For pilot typically customers choose hosted with a private VPC peering or Dedicated depending on throughput and policy.
[01:47] Marco Ruiz: We prefer a private VPC or dedicated; our compliance team doesn't want inference traffic traversing public multi-tenant endpoints for the pilot.
[01:56] Priya Nandi: Understood. For private deployment we'll provide a customer-managed VPC setup and you can manage keys via your KMS/HSM. For dedicated we can offer reserved pools with network isolation.
[02:08] Ethan Cole: For benchmarks we want both cold-start (empty KV cache) and warm-cache numbers, and breakdowns by sequence length. Also GPU details — which instances and NVLink etc.
[02:19] Priya Nandi: We'll include both. Our benchmark doc will show A100/H100 memory footprints, batch sizes, and perf delta with quantized variants.
[02:28] Anya Patel: From compliance perspective, main questions: SOC 2 Type II status and report, ISO27001 certification if you have it, penetration test cadence, vulnerability scanning, and who holds keys.
[02:38] Jordan Hale: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in-scope — we can share the security pack; ISO27001 summary as applicable, and we do periodic pentests and internal scans. Keys can be customer-managed in the private deployments — we support KMS integrations.
[02:51] Marco Ruiz: Can you share an attestation or the report? We will need evidence for procurement.
[02:55] Jordan Hale: We'll upload the SOC2 bundle to the shared S3 link and mark it confidential — Jordan: action item to upload by Friday.
[03:04] Priya Nandi: On RBAC — Redwood Console supports role-based access and token scoping. For pilot we recommend RBAC roles for SRE, Security, and App. Audit logs record API keys, route calls, and admin actions with timestamps.
[03:17] Anya Patel: Do audit logs include requester IP, masked payloads, and the model variant used?
[03:22] Priya Nandi: We include requester metadata, route, token ID, and we can enable payload redaction for PII. Model variant and runtime metadata are in the logs. Retention is configurable; default is 90 days for hosted, longer for enterprise add-ons.
[03:36] Ethan Cole: For the pilot we need 180 days retention and the ability to export logs to our SIEM (we use Splunk). Can you do forwarding via secure syslog or S3 export?
[03:48] Priya Nandi: Yes, we can forward logs to your S3 bucket or via secure channels — we'll include Splunk forwarding guide.
[03:55] Marco Ruiz: On networking, do you support private peering and enforce TLS everywhere?
[03:59] Jordan Hale: Yes, TLS in transit everywhere, mutual TLS options for dedicated/private, and support for VPC peering and private endpoints.
[04:09] Anya Patel: SCIM for provisioning/SSO integration timeline? We want SAML 2.0 and SCIM to provision groups so RBAC maps to our IdP.
[04:17] Priya Nandi: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for group sync. For pilot we can enable SSO integration and a SAML test connection. Full SCIM provisioning might be post-pilot depending on integration timeline.
[04:29] Jordan Hale: Ok let's pivot to success criteria and benchmark targets — Priya?
[04:34] Priya Nandi: Proposed gates: 1) Functional: API correctness across 3 sample prompts and deterministic output checks for reranking flows. 2) Performance: p95 latency <200ms for median seq lengths at pilot traffic; sustained 1.5k r/min with burst handling. 3) Reliability: <1% error rate and graceful fallback to smaller model variants. 4) Security: SOC2 docs reviewed, SSO working for at least two users, RBAC roles validated, audit logs exported.
[04:58] Ethan Cole: For cost we want rough unit economics — cost per 1k tokens served (approx). We'll look at Redwood Optimize recommendations after benchmarks.
[05:07] Priya Nandi: We'll produce a cost model. Benchmarks will include token throughput, tokens/sec, and cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated sizing.
[05:16] Marco Ruiz: What about PII — we cannot have user messages persist in logs or be used for training.
[05:21] Jordan Hale: Redwood never uses customer payloads for model training by default; for hosted we can guarantee no training use and support a no-retention policy for PII in logs. We'll put that in the pilot SOW.
[05:33] Anya Patel: Need confirmation in writing — legal will want a clause.
[05:36] Jordan Hale: We'll include explicit non-training and data residency clauses.
[05:40] Priya Nandi: Back to benchmarks — we'll run load tests with a test harness. Ethan, can you provide a sample trace?
[05:45] Ethan Cole: Yes, I'll provide a 24-hour trace representing diurnal pattern and a 1-hour stress trace showing burst behaviour.
[05:51] Priya Nandi: Perfect. We'll run three scenarios: smoke (low qps), steady-state (your expected baseline), and stress bursts. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, error rates, and GPU utilization.
[06:04] Marco Ruiz: For dedicated sizing any guidance on how many GPUs for sustained 2k r/min?
[06:10] Priya Nandi: Depends on model — for a 13B family model with quantized runtime you might fit on 1-2 A100s for moderate concurrency, but for production you may want 2-4 GPUs with autoscaling. We'll provide recommended configs in the benchmark report.
[06:23] Anya Patel: What about model fallbacks when a node is unhealthy — automatic routing?
[06:27] Jordan Hale: Smart routing will fallback to compatible model variants based on policy. We'll demonstrate failover in the pilot.
[06:35] Ethan Cole: How do we validate RBAC controls end-to-end? We want an SRE to attempt an unauthorized call and ensure logs show the denial.
[06:42] Priya Nandi: We'll include an RBAC test plan: attempt role-scoped actions, confirm errors, and verify logs show requester, action, and response.
[06:50] Marco Ruiz: Timeline — what are realistic dates? We want pilot running in two weeks and finishing in four weeks.
[06:55] Jordan Hale: Proposed: share SOW + SOC2 by 2026-04-16; you share workload traces by 2026-04-18; we run initial benchmark week of 2026-04-27; pilot kickoff week of 2026-05-04 for 4 weeks. That meets a 4-week execution window.
[07:10] Anya Patel: Procurement also needs contract language around breach notification and data residency.
[07:14] Jordan Hale: We'll flag legal to include breach notification timelines and EU data residency options.
[07:19] Priya Nandi: A few gotchas to note — in hosted multi-tenant there are default retention policies. For strict control we recommend dedicated or private deployment. Also SCIM provisioning may take extra time if your IdP requires custom claims.
[07:33] Ethan Cole: For the bench harness, can you supply Dockerized runner and instructions for running against a dedicated pool?
[07:39] Priya Nandi: Yes, we'll share the runner and test harness repo. We'll also provide a sample k8s job for load generation.
[07:47] Marco Ruiz: Security question — do you provide per-tenant encryption keys for hosted customers?
[07:52] Jordan Hale: Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys available on enterprise plans. Private deployments can use your own KMS/HSM.
[07:59] Anya Patel: Pen test evidence timeline? We may want to run a light pen test against the pilot environment.
[08:04] Jordan Hale: We can coordinate a scoped test; we'll require a test plan and timebox. We do advise a joint ops window.
[08:12] Priya Nandi: Quick note on audit logs: we can provide immutable logs for admin actions and export a digest for compliance review.
[08:20] Anya Patel: Good. One more thing: retention policies for backups and model weights — do you retain any customer artifacts beyond logs?
[08:27] Jordan Hale: We only retain model artifacts as part of hosting the model; for private deployments you control model weights. We'll document retention.
[08:36] Ethan Cole: On acceptance, do you accept our pass/fail criteria or recommend thresholds?
[08:40] Priya Nandi: We'll propose thresholds but they'll be jointly agreed and documented in the SOW.
[08:46] Marco Ruiz: Anything else on compliance — SOC2 subservice orgs or third party subproc?
[08:50] Jordan Hale: We'll list subprocessors; also provide an attestation for third-party infra components.
[08:56] Anya Patel: Ok — to summarize the action items.
[09:00] Jordan Hale: Quick recap: Redwood sends SOC2 + ISO evidence and SOW; Redwood shares benchmark plan and test harness; Ibex sends workload traces; both agree on pilot dates with a kickoff first week of May. We'll draft RBAC test cases and log export config. Any open questions?
[09:19] Marco Ruiz: Nope sounds good. Thanks.
[09:22] Jordan Hale: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with Confluence links and the SOW draft.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps and filler words removed for readability; some product terms may be mistranscribed (K V cache vs KV cache).

End of transcript.
